name: Roblox

Software Engineer.dsaDepth: Heavy — a genuinely unusual 2-hour OA mixing LeetCode coding with proprietary game-based puzzle tasks and a 25-minute behavioral section, then a coding-focused phone screen
rounds: Recruiter screen (~30 min): background, motivation, in-office policy and comp alignment

Online assessment (~2 hrs, CodeSignal/HackerRank plus Roblox’s own platform): standard coding problems, proprietary game-based challenges (e.g. build-a-car, factory-optimization puzzles — described as fluid-intelligence tests, not pattern-matchable), and a dedicated 25-min situational-judgment section
Technical phone screen (60-90 min): coding for junior/mid, project deep-dive and architecture for senior

Onsite loop (4+ hrs): further coding (medium-hard, LeetCode-pattern, with follow-ups anchored to Roblox features, e.g. designing a Robux escrow system instead of a generic payment system), system design (massive concurrent-user scale, Lua performance, engine efficiency)
Bar Raiser round (~60 min): system design plus behavioral, run by a calibrated outside interviewer
extraTopics: The game-based OA sections — described by multiple candidates as the single biggest surprise/filter in the whole process
Comfort with ambiguity: interviewers reportedly give minimal guidance and expect candidates to drive problems independently
Anchoring generic algorithms to Roblox-specific product scenarios (payments, UGC, concurrency at scale)
Software Engineer.notes: Process length is reported as 4-6 weeks typically, with some candidates reporting up to 3 months.
